- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is positive — apply a 1-2 day lag correction downward.
- In mean-reversion scenarios (sentiment oscillating), model frequently overcorrects — dampen forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price if recent sentiment is bullish and price is trending up — adjust upward by 1–3% of recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.33), model often fails to capture short-term volatility — add 0.5–1.5% buffer for sudden moves.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags — forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if sentiment is positive but price is trending down, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid false peaks.
